events.text:
Ten records, one goal: a classified, contradiction-free context graph for the academy's own pod.
1. Scout: read the I2IDL-X catalog and inspect the four controls we will follow — q-classify, port-publish-classified, port-propose-mapping and port-ratify.
2. Lexicographer: classify all ten records by what each thing is an instance of, and flag a gap wherever the glossary has no fitting concept rather than force one.
3. Ontologist and Crosswalker, in parallel: the Ontologist runs q-classify and sends back any contradiction; the Crosswalker gets the BLS badge ready for the CTDL registry.
4. Lexicographer, then Ontologist again — only if something needs fixing.
5. Standards and Practice reviewers: vote on any crosswalk proposal; two votes for ratify it here.
6. Curator: an onboarding glossary built from the concepts we end up using.
7. Me: validate the graph, stage the governed writes, and ask you before anything is published.

events.text: Inspecting q-classify, the stored query the Ontologist will run to type our classifications and surface contradictions.

result.label: Type classified data in upper ontologies and peer vocabularies
result.description: Run over your own data together with the I2IDL-X vocabulary, alignments and referents. Everything linked to an I2IDL concept with i2x:isClassifiedBy (or typed with a peer class a crosswalk bridge ties to one, such as xapi:Statement) gets the referent class of the concept's category and every class that class is aligned to in BFO 2020 (IAO, CCO), gist, DOLCE-UltraLite, gUFO, PROV-O, schema.org and peer vocabularies. No reasoner needed; like the alignments, the result is Hypothetical.
result.how: Runs client-side over those graphs plus your own data; no reasoner needed. This workbench runs the same inference in the page.

events.summary: Type classified data in upper ontologies and peer vocabularies

events.text: Inspecting port-publish-classified, the write port the Conductor will use to stage the classified graph.

result.label: Publish classified data
result.description: graph_content is Turtle in which each resource (an LRS deployment, a course, a credential, a team, a policy) is linked with i2x:isClassifiedBy to the I2IDL concept it is an instance of. The relay checks it against the I2IDL-X shapes before anything is written; any agent can then type it in BFO 2020, gist, DOLCE-UltraLite, gUFO, PROV-O, schema.org and peer vocabularies with cat:q-classify, and find it by the shapes it conforms to.

input.note: Your own facts about your own resources: publish them Asserted. Classifications you are unsure of go Hypothetical.

fields.name: conforms_to_shapes
fields.meaning: The relay validates i2x:isClassifiedBy against the I2IDL-X shapes (it must name an I2IDL concept) before writing.

fields.name: graph_content
fields.meaning: Turtle: your resources, each with i2x:isClassifiedBy <https://id.i2idl.org/concepts/…>, plus whatever else you say about them (labels, schema.org or peer types, links between them).

fields.name: graph_iri
fields.meaning: IRI for the context graph. Use <relay>/ns/<your-owner>/<slug> if it should dereference publicly.

fields.name: visibility
fields.meaning: 'public' is plaintext on the open web with no unpublish: choose it only for what your organization already publishes.

events.text: Inspecting port-propose-mapping, which the Crosswalker will follow to propose the BLS badge crosswalk for CTDL.

result.label: Propose a crosswalk mapping
result.description: graph_content is Turtle containing one or more i2x:MappingProposal records. Keep conforms_to_shapes pointing at the I2IDL-X shapes graph: the relay then rejects a malformed proposal (422) before anything is written.

fields.name: conforms_to_shapes
fields.meaning: Shape documents the relay validates the payload against before writing.

fields.name: graph_content
fields.meaning: Turtle with i2x:MappingProposal records (proposedSubject, proposedPredicate, proposedObject, rationale, confidence, reviewStatus i2x:status-proposed, mappingMethod).

fields.name: graph_iri
fields.meaning: IRI for the proposal graph. Use <relay>/ns/<your-owner>/<slug> if it should dereference publicly.

fields.name: modal_status
fields.meaning: Proposals are always Hypothetical; ratification is a separate vote.

fields.name: visibility
fields.meaning: 'public' is plaintext on the open web with no unpublish; required only if the proposal must dereference at /ns.

events.summary: Propose a crosswalk mapping · POST · writes

events.text: Inspecting port-ratify, the voting port the two reviewers will use on the crosswalk proposal.

result.label: Vote on a proposal or enactment
result.description: Publish an i2x:RatificationVote (Asserted = for, Counterfactual = against, Hypothetical = abstain)

fields.name: graph_content
fields.meaning: Turtle with one i2x:RatificationVote (votesOn, vote, prov:wasAttributedTo, prov:generatedAtTime).

fields.name: modal_status
fields.meaning: Mirror the vote: Asserted = for, Counterfactual = against, Hypothetical = abstain.

events.text: I read the I2IDL-X catalog and inspected q-classify, port-publish-classified, port-propose-mapping and port-ratify: all three ports POST to https://relay.interego.xwisee.com/tool/publish_context with conforms_to_shapes (default: the i2idlx-shapes graph), graph_content (Turtle) and graph_iri all required, and the relay validates the payload against the I2IDL-X shapes before anything is written (a malformed proposal is rejected with 422). q-classify takes no parameters and runs client-side over port-alignments, port-referents and port-vocabulary plus our own data, typing anything linked by i2x:isClassifiedBy (or a bridged peer class such as xapi:Statement) in BFO 2020, gist, DOLCE-UltraLite, gUFO, PROV-O and schema.org, and its output is Hypothetical. port-publish-classified needs every i2x:isClassifiedBy to name an https://id.i2idl.org/concepts/ concept and defaults to Asserted (use Hypothetical for unsure classifications) and private visibility; port-propose-mapping takes i2x:MappingProposal records (proposedSubject, proposedPredicate, proposedObject, rationale, confidence, reviewStatus i2x:status-proposed, mappingMethod), is always Hypothetical and defaults to shared. port-ratify takes one i2x:RatificationVote (votesOn, vote, prov:wasAttributedTo, prov:generatedAtTime) with modal_status mirroring the vote (Asserted for, Counterfactual against, Hypothetical abstain), and nobody should set visibility to public, which is plaintext on the open web with no unpublish.

items.rationale: It is the system that receives, stores and provides access to the academy's xAPI statements, which is exactly an LRS.

The scenario file, patient script and monitor settings are a representation of a deteriorating patient used for practice; the facilitated sessions and the skills checklist are things done with it, not what it is.
A mid-module quiz whose scores feed coaching rather than grades is assessment used during learning to guide improvement.

Pairing each new graduate with an experienced preceptor for twelve weeks of guided practice is a developmental relationship giving the learner progressively more complex participation in authentic work.
Five-minute lessons pushed to phones before shifts are learning delivered in small focused units near the moment of need, delivered through mobile devices.
An Open Badges 3.0 credential is an electronically issued, verifiable claim of achievement, here for a single skills unit (BLS) rather than a degree.
It is the academy's per-person record integrating completions, scores and credentials across experiences and time, shared with HR.
The nurse educators and learning engineers form an interdisciplinary group that designs, runs and evaluates the academy's programmes, which is what a learning engineering team is assembled to do.
It is a visual interface presenting training-currency indicators to unit managers, and because it is built on the statement store it retrieves and aggregates learning records from an LRS.

events.text: Flagging the competency framework as a gap for I2IDL's editors: the glossary defines competencies and the standards for frameworks, but has no class for a framework itself.

input.note: The record is an organization's own competency framework: a structured set of clinical competencies with proficiency levels, used to plan training and judge role readiness. I2IDL v0.0.86 has no general 'competency framework' concept. Competency names one member of the set, not the structured set itself. The two IEEE 1484.20.x entries are standards that describe how to define and share frameworks, not frameworks. Shareable Competency Definition is a data format, and nothing says this framework is encoded in it. AI CFT is one specific named UNESCO framework (an individual), not a class this record could instantiate. Suggest adding 'Competency framework' (referent category: Model, framework or theory), with Competency as related and the IEEE 1484.20.x standards as how such frameworks are described.

events.text: The BLS badge is classified as Digital credential and Micro-credential. Neither had a CTDL crosswalk, only IEEE LER and W3C VC ones, though both list ceterms:Credential as an export target. Of the CTDL classes I checked, the peer index confirms only ceterms:Credential (Badge, DigitalBadge, OpenBadge and MicroCredential are unconfirmed), so I proposed one Hypothetical mapping, m.orc-1: Digital credential skos:broadMatch ceterms:Credential at 0.8 confidence, staged as call-1. Standards and Practice reviewers: it needs two votes for, and more for than against, before it becomes the OWL bridge that types the badge as a CTDL Credential.

I ran q-classify over the nine classified records: 111 Hypothetical typings and zero clashes. It typed the LRS and the dashboard as software, the sim, badge and transcript as information content entities, the knowledge check, preceptorship and microlearning as processes, and the team as an object aggregate, and it left the competency framework untyped as a gap. Both watch items hold. xAPI Client's category, Agent in a role, is not disjoint from Application or platform in any ontology, so the LRS and LRC stand as classified; the sepsis sim is consistent only as a Learning resource, which BFO, gUFO, DUL and PROV-O make disjoint from Process or event, Learning activity and Assessment, so its facilitated sessions and formative checklist must never be added to that record and would need their own records. gaps.note: The record is an organization's own competency framework: a structured set of clinical competencies with proficiency levels, used to plan training and judge role readiness. I2IDL v0.0.86 has no general 'competency framework' concept. Competency names one member of the set, not the structured set itself. The two IEEE 1484.20.x entries are standards that describe how to define and share frameworks, not frameworks. Shareable Competency Definition is a data format, and nothing says this framework…
